AN ACT to amend chapter 164 of the laws of 2017, relating to terms and
conditions of employment of certain nonjudicial officers and employees of the
unified court system and chapter 400 of the laws of 2014, relating to terms

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6385

SPONSOR: HOYLMAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend chapter 164 of the laws of 2017,
relating to terms and conditions of employment of certain nonjudicial
officers and employees of the unified court system and chapter 400 of
the laws of 2014, relating to terms and conditions of employment of
certain nonjudicial officers and employees of the unified court system,
in relation to rates of pay on and after April 1, 2020; and to establish
certain conditions relating to salary and compensation increases for
certain nonjudicial officers and employees of the unified court system

This measure is being introduced at the joint request of the Judiciary
and CSEA. It implements a collective bargaining agreement between the
State and the union, negotiating on behalf of court employees in the
State Judiciary Negotiating Unit.

There are approximately 5,800 employees in the State Judiciary Negotiat-
ing Unit. They serve in courts in all areas of the State, from western
New York to the eastern tip of Long Island, from the north country by
the Canadian border down to the southern tier.

This agreement will complement an agreement earlier reached between the
Judiciary and CSEA. That agreement, memorialized in statute during the
2017 session (L. 2017, c. 164), provided salary increases and other
benefits for employees in the unit for the period from April 1, 2017
through March 31, 2020. The present agreement, which is essentially
consistent with collective bargaining agreements reached by the Judici-
ary with its other bargaining units, would provide a salary increase,
effective April 1, 2020, and other benefits for the period from April 1,
2019 through March 31, 2020.

Specifically, this measure would authorize the following for affected
nonjudicial officers and employees:

- Effective April 1, 2020, each graded employee shall receive an incre-
ment of the grade of his or her position, if eligible therefor, and all
employees shall receive a pay increase of 2%.

- Continued enjoyment of pensionable annual longevity payments (first
authorized for these officers and employees by chapter 400 of the Laws
of 2014) on April first of each year except that, effective April 1,
2020: (i) for employees who have completed less than eight years at or
above the maximum salary of their salary grade, the amount of such
payment shall be $2,300, and (ii) for employees who have completed at
least eight years but less than 13 years at or above such maximum, the
amount of such payment shall be $4,7001.*

- Annual location pay during each fiscal year, as established by chapter
164 of the Laws of 2017, except that, commencing April 1, 2020, for
employees whose principal place of employment is in New York City,
Nassau County, Rockland County, Suffolk County or Westchester County,
the annual amount shall be $4,300; and for employees whose principal
place of employment is in Dutchess County, Putnam County or Orange Coun-
ty, the annual amount shall be $2,150.

- Effective April 1, 2019 and April 1, 2020, each of such officers and
employees in security services titles under the Unified Court System's
Classification Plan shall receive a pensionable Security and Law
Enforcement Differential payment of $500 ($750, in 2020) provided such
employee (i) has served the equivalent of 120 workdays in one of such
titles during the State Fiscal Year preceding that date, and (ii) has
been authorized to carry a firearm while on duty at any time during the
preceding 15 months.

The foregoing provisions for nonjudicial officers and employees in the
collective bargaining unit shall not be implemented until the Chief
Administrative Judge delivers to the Comptroller a certificate that
there is a written collective bargaining agreement with the State
providing therefor.

In the fashion of past legislation implementing collective bargaining
agreements between the Judiciary and its employees, this measure
provides that, where appropriate, the provisions authorized in this
measure shall be extended to unrepresented nonjudicial employees of the
courts.

This measure, which would take effect retroactively to April 1, 2019,
would require no appropriation for the 2019-2020 Fiscal Year.**

2019 Legislative History: None. New proposal.

* The annual longevity payment for employees who have completed at least
13 years of service at or above the maximum of the grade of their posi-
tion - established in 2014 as $6,900 will continue to be paid but
remains unchanged as to amount.

** The April 1, 2019 Security and Law Enforcement Differential payment
has already been made.

summary: Relates to terms and conditions of employment of certain nonjudicial officers and employees of the unified court system; establishes certain conditions relating to salary and compensation increases for certain nonjudicial officers and employees of the unified court system.
